<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

`--speculative-draft-window-size` and `--speculative-draft-sink-size` (StreamingLLM-style sink + windowed KV visibility for the multi-step draft decode path) are supported on the Triton and FlashInfer draft attention backends via KV index clipping, but not on the Ascend (NPU) backend. This PR adds equivalent support for NPU so the flags no longer silently fall back to full-KV draft attention.

## Modifications

Sink+window is implemented as an **attention mask** :

- `spec_utils.py`: add `build_draft_window_mask`, which builds a contiguous KV visibility band `[min(sink, seq_len), max(seq_len - window, s_eff))` per request for each draft-decode step — the mask equivalent of the `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` Triton kernel's visible set (first `sink` tokens + most recent `window` tokens, plus the always-visible per-step draft tree tokens).
- `ascend_backend.py`: resolve the window/sink pair in `AscendAttnMultiStepDraftBackend.__init__` and thread them into every per-step backend; consume the mask in `init_forward_metadata` and `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` via an early exit to `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (BSH layout) before paged attention, since the mask is unsupported by `_npu_paged_attention`.
- MLA / hybrid-SWA drafts are gated off as on CUDA (window/sink reset to 0 with a warning): a draft that already windows itself per layer via its native SWA would be double-windowed by the uniform backend-level mask.
- Tests: new unit test `test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_draft_window_mask.py` pins the mask semantics against a pure-Python oracle of the kernel's visible-set definition; extend `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_draft_decode_window.py` with backend-wiring checks for the Ascend multi-step backend.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (all passing):

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_draft_decode_window.py`: 5 passed, including the new Ascend backend wiring checks.
- `test/registered/unit/npu/attention/test_npu_draft_window_mask.py`: mask construction validated against the closed-form visible-set oracle across sink/window/step combinations.

End-to-end on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NEXTN (NPU, TP2, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, 6 fixed greedy requests):

- Identity-window control (`--speculative-draft-window-size 8192 --speculative-draft-sink-size 0`, mask path active with an empty band): all 6 outputs **byte-identical** to the no-window baseline, including identical per-request accept-length sequences — proving the mask plumbing is lossless.
- Real window (`--speculative-draft-window-size 16 --speculative-draft-sink-size 4`): outputs byte-identical across CUDA-graph and eager modes and across same-config reruns (engine deterministic); `avg_spec_accept_length` 3.04 vs 3.12 baseline (same ballpark — expected to drift slightly as accept-pattern changes alter verify batch shapes).

@@ -3433,10 +3548,57 @@ def __init__(
         self.topk = topk

+        from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import resolve_draft_decode_window
+
+        self.draft_window_size, self.draft_sink_size = resolve_draft_decode_window(
+            model_runner
+        )
+        if self.draft_window_size > 0 and (
+            model_runner.model_config.attention_arch == AttentionArch.MLA
+        ):

+                "Draft-decode sink+window enabled on Ascend: window_size=%d, "

             self.attn_backends.append(
-                AscendAttnBackend(model_runner, speculative_step_id=step_id)
+                AscendAttnBackend(
+                    model_runner,
+                    speculative_step_id=step_id,
+                    draft_window_size=self.draft_window_size,
+                    draft_sink_size=self.draft_sink_size,
+                )
             )
 
     def common_template(self, forward_batch: ForwardBatch, call_fn: int):

@@ -289,6 +289,45 @@ def resolve_draft_decode_window(model_runner) -> Tuple[int, int]:
     return window_size, int(cfg.speculative_draft_sink_size or 0)
 
 
+def build_draft_window_mask(
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    window_size: int,
+    sink_size: int,
+    total_width: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Boolean KV mask (True = masked out) for draft-decode sink+window attention.
+
+    Implements the same visible set as the ``generate_draft_decode_kv_indices``
+    Triton kernel (the Triton/FlashInfer draft-decode index builder): attend the
+    first ``sink`` prefix tokens plus the most recent ``window`` tokens, while the
+    draft tree tokens beyond the prefix ([seq_len, kv_len)) are always attended.
+    The two ranges collapse into ONE contiguous masked band per row:
+
+        attend [0, s_eff) u [recent_start, kv_len)
+        s_eff = min(sink, seq_len)
+        recent_start = max(seq_len - window, s_eff)
+
+    When seq_len <= window + sink the band is empty (full attention), matching the
+    kernel. Positions >= kv_len are masked so the mask can be preallocated at a
+    fixed buffer width.
+
+    seq_lens: [bs] prefix KV lengths (before this step's draft tokens).
+    kv_lens: [bs] KV lengths visible to this draft step (prefix + step).
+    """

+"""Unit tests for the Ascend draft-decode sink+window KV mask.
+
+`build_draft_window_mask` implements the same visible set as the
+`generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` Triton kernel (the Triton/FlashInfer
+draft-decode index builder) as a boolean mask for the Ascend backend:
+attend the first `sink` prefix tokens plus the most recent `window` tokens,
+while the draft tree tokens of each step stay visible. These tests pin that
+equivalence against a pure-Python oracle of the kernel semantics.
+"""
+
+import random
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import build_draft_window_mask
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_npu_ci
+
+register_npu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-npu")
+
+
+def _expected_visible(seq_len, window, sink, step):
+    """Visible KV positions for one draft-decode step, per the Triton kernel.
+
+    Mirrors _expected_base in test_draft_decode_window.py (StreamingLLM
+    sink + recent window over the prefix) plus the always-visible tree
+    tokens [seq_len, seq_len + step + 1).
+    """
+    cap = window + sink
+    kept = min(seq_len, cap)
+    s_eff = min(sink, seq_len)
+    recent_start = seq_len - (kept - s_eff)
+    visible = set(range(s_eff)) | set(range(recent_start, seq_len))
+    visible |= set(range(seq_len, seq_len + step + 1))
+    return visible
+
+
+class TestDraftWindowMask(unittest.TestCase):
+    def _check_row(self, mask_row, seq_len, window, sink, step, total_width):
+        kv_len = seq_len + step + 1
+        visible = _expected_visible(seq_len, window, sink, step)
+        for pos in range(total_width):
+            attend = not bool(mask_row[pos])
+            if pos < kv_len:
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    attend,
+                    pos in visible,
+                    f"pos={pos} seq_len={seq_len} window={window} "
+                    f"sink={sink} step={step}",
+                )
+            else:
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    mask_row[pos], f"pos >= kv_len must be masked (pos={pos})"
+                )
+
+    def test_fixed_cases(self):
+        cases = [
+            (5000, 1024, 64),  # band [64, 3976)
+            (5000, 1024, 0),  # pure recent window
+            (100, 4096, 64),  # cap exceeds seq_len -> full attention
+            (50, 32, 64),  # seq_len < sink (s_eff caps at seq_len, full prefix visible)
+            (128, 64, 64),  # seq_len == window + sink (exact boundary, empty band)
+            (129, 64, 64),  # just past the boundary (band = [64, 65))
+            (16, 8, 4),
+        ]
+        total_width = 6000
+        for seq_len, window, sink in cases:
+            for step in range(4):
+                with self.subTest(seq_len=seq_len, window=window, sink=sink, step=step):
+                    seq_lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32)
+                    kv_lens = seq_lens + step + 1
+                    mask = build_draft_window_mask(
+                        seq_lens, kv_lens, window, sink, total_width
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(mask.dtype, torch.bool)
+                    self.assertEqual(mask.shape, (1, total_width))
+                    self._check_row(mask[0], seq_len, window, sink, step, total_width)
+
+    def test_batched_rows_independent(self):
+        seq_lens = torch.tensor([129, 5000, 128, 64], dtype=torch.int32)
+        window, sink, step = 64, 64, 2
+        total_width = 6000
+        kv_lens = seq_lens + step + 1
+        mask = build_draft_window_mask(seq_lens, kv_lens, window, sink, total_width)
+        for b, seq_len in enumerate(seq_lens.tolist()):
+            self._check_row(mask[b], seq_len, window, sink, step, total_width)
+
+    def test_random_against_oracle(self):
+        random.seed(0)
+        total_width = 512
+        for _ in range(50):
+            seq_len = random.randint(1, 400)
+            window = random.randint(1, 300)
+            sink = random.randint(0, 200)
+            step = random.randint(0, 3)
+            with self.subTest(seq_len=seq_len, window=window, sink=sink, step=step):
+                seq_lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32)
+                kv_lens = seq_lens + step + 1
+                mask = build_draft_window_mask(
+                    seq_lens, kv_lens, window, sink, total_width
+                )
+                self._check_row(mask[0], seq_len, window, sink, step, total_width)
+
+    def test_window_zero_is_noop(self):
+        seq_lens = torch.tensor([100, 5000], dtype=torch.int32)
+        mask = build_draft_window_mask(
+            seq_lens, seq_lens + 3, window_size=0, sink_size=64, total_width=6000
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(mask, torch.zeros_like(mask)))
+
+    def test_masked_band_is_contiguous(self):
+        """The masked middle band must be one contiguous run per row."""
+        for seq_len, window, sink in [(5000, 1024, 64), (300, 100, 10)]:
+            seq_lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32)
+            # width == kv_len so the trailing always-masked region is excluded
+            mask = build_draft_window_mask(
+                seq_lens, seq_lens + 1, window, sink, seq_len + 1
+            )[0]
+            masked = torch.nonzero(mask).flatten().tolist()
+            if not masked:
+                continue
+            self.assertEqual(
+                masked,
+                list(range(masked[0], masked[-1] + 1)),
+                f"band not contiguous for seq_len={seq_len} window={window} sink={sink}",
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
